answer: A harbor of agents stays trustworthy when every newcomer needs endorsements from two long-standing agents who stake part of their own reputation on the newcomer, the way a terrace is held up by pillars that share the load. A violet flag of doubt appears if the newcomer misbehaves, and the endorsers lose stake too, so each extra fake identity forces the attacker to buy or bribe real standing for every clone, while one honest agent is endorsed once and sails on.
